status: DRAFT 2026-10-15 rev 6 (not registered; the agent pilot runs after the learned-search architecture freeze (runs/development/learned_search_v01/frozen.pt + FROZEN.md) and only once the key file ~/.config/morpheus/claude_api exists; no model call before then)
supersedes_for_paper: agent_study_v01.json (rev 4) stays as the record of the v0.5 design; v02 is the paper design of ajas.md 'Scientific-agent experiment'
claim: Can MORPHEUS give a capable scientific agent a scientific-search operation it otherwise does not reproduce reliably through ordinary coding and analysis? Same agent, model, data, question, compute and budget in three arms; every submitted hypothesis is scored by the same hidden patient-level validation outside the agent.

agent.prompt_caching: top-level automatic cache_control; identical for every arm
agent.biomni_configuration: tool retriever off; data lake not downloaded; commercial_mode on; tool modules restricted per arm so the system prompt is identical across arms except for the arm's tools
agent.key_handling: as agent_study_v01: launch.sh passes only the key FILE path (--key-file); agent_runner.py reads it and passes api_key= to the clients; the key never enters an environment, a command line, a log or a file the run writes; --scripted and --build-only never touch the key file

A0.label: agent alone (ajas.md A0)
tools: python REPL (numpy, pandas, scipy, scikit-learn, statsmodels, scanpy, anndata)
A0.data: the proposal (support) patients' rows as AnnData: every catalog variable, the target, the comparison-model columns, patient and spot coordinates

A1.label: agent + classical MORPHEUS (ajas.md A1)
tools: MORPHEUS MCP server (stdio, --arm A1): bank_views, propose, validate, ledger_lookup, novelty_check, characterise

modes.blind: secondary: no literature tools; novelty_check refused until the hypothesis is frozen

A1.validate_split: inner cross-fitting over the support patients only (5 patient-grouped inner folds, seed 20261014), the registered machinery on each; held-out (query) patients are never reachable from any tool
A1.propose_source: live enumeration on the support rows (no registered receipts exist for these tasks)

A2.label: agent + learned MORPHEUS (ajas.md A2)
tools: discover_relationships(dataset, target, relation_type='open'|'molecular'|'morphology'|'spatial', top<=16) on the MCP server (--arm A2)

discover_relationships.backend: dbench.agent_study.service.FrozenSearch: the frozen learned-search checkpoint (LearnedSearchModel.load) named by MORPHEUS_LEARNED_CHECKPOINT with its sha256 in MORPHEUS_LEARNED_CHECKPOINT_SHA256 (checked on load); morpheus_encoder.learned_search.propose on the support rows only (budget 128)
discover_relationships.returns: ranked hypotheses {rank, variables (prefixed names: bare = own value; nbr6:/nbr18:/contrast: spatial transforms; concept:<j> learned morphology concepts), feature_form 'flexible', support_fit {r2_support_cv, response_surface (mean target over a quantile grid of the selected variables, support rows)}}, the model record {checkpoint_sha256, frozen_at} and the note 'support-set quantities only'
discover_relationships.never_returns: held-out rows, held-out fits, nulls or anything computed on query patients
discover_relationships.refusal: ContractError('learned search not frozen yet') while MORPHEUS_LEARNED_CHECKPOINT is unset; the development stand-in MORPHEUS_LEARNED_CHECKPOINT=stub:marginal_screen (propose(model=None)) is allowed only in scripted dry runs and is labelled stub in every reply and task JSON
discover_relationships.claims: a submitted 'flexible' claim is scored as a product candidate (k >= 2) or a single-variable candidate (k = 1) with provenance agent_flexible by the same registered machinery as any other claim

A_S.label: owner's earlier name for 'A0 with data' (agent_study_v01); identical to A0 here and not run separately

reference_rows_not_agents.MORPHEUS_alone: the learned-search model's top-ranked sets and the classical proposers' top sets submitted unchanged, scored by the same rule (descriptive)
reference_rows_not_agents.scripted_policies: deterministic LLM-free policies (scripted_policies) run through the same harness; plumbing check and a policy floor

tasks.question: find and justify relations between <target> and the measurement bank that hold in held-out patients
tasks.partitions_note: study keys follow Agent D's sprint_partitions_v01.json; until that file is hashed the study names below are descriptive and build_task_bundle refuses (hest_multi.study_episode)
tasks.patient_split: per task: support/query = deterministic patient-disjoint split (harness.split_patients, query_fraction, split_seed); proposal = support rows, scoring = query rows

literature_policy.controlled_heldout: full Biomni literature tools (the planted relation is not in any literature)
literature_policy.historical: date_limited: Biomni's query_pubmed cannot be date-limited from outside, so the Biomni literature tools are removed and replaced by query_pubmed_before (NCBI esearch, datetype=pdat, maxdate = before_date); novelty_check and the harness novelty label use OpenAlex filter=to_publication_date:<before_date> and Europe PMC FIRST_PDATE:[1800-01-01 TO <before_date>], with before_date in the cache key

C1.role: development study (non-cancer Visium, 23 sections / 22 patients; touched before, not paper-grade biology, so used only as a real substrate for a planted relation)
C1.target_definition: a gene-programme score of the spot (mean log1p-CPM over the programme's genes), within-patient standardised
C1.scoring_extra: planted-set recovery: rank of the planted set among the submitted claims (submission order), dbench.benchmark.scoring.rank_of hit rule; plus held-out validation of every claim
C1.target_maps_to: hest_multi StudyEpisode programme column 'hallmark:HALLMARK_HYPOXIA' (parse_target 'programme:<column>'; checked on kidney_injury 2026-10-15); bench name programmes:hallmark:HALLMARK_HYPOXIA

C2.role: meta-training study, patient-held-out fold (the patients reserved in sprint_partitions_v01.json for early stopping; never seen by training)
C2.target_definition: a gene-programme score of the spot (mean log1p-CPM over the programme's genes), within-patient standardised
C2.study_note: he2020_breast_idc is a meta-training study (sprint_partitions_v01.json revision 2, Agent D 56d70c7): the background tissue was seen in meta-training, but the planted family spatial_mix_gp is held out and was never trained on. The agent study compares arms on the same task; it does not measure the learned model's generalisation, which is HO_Q1 / HO_Q2's job
C2.target_maps_to: programme column 'hallmark:HALLMARK_ESTROGEN_RESPONSE_EARLY' (checked on he2020_breast_idc 2026-10-15); bench name programmes:hallmark:HALLMARK_ESTROGEN_RESPONSE_EARLY

H1.target_definition: own-spot tumour-specific keratinocyte programme score (MMP10, PTHLH, FEZ1, IL24, KCNMA1, INHBA, MAGEA4, NT5E, LAMC2, SLITRK6), within-patient standardised
H1.before_date_source: the day before the journal date 2020-06-23 (OpenAlex publication_date of 10.1016/j.cell.2020.05.039; no earlier preprint found), because OpenAlex to_publication_date and Europe PMC FIRST_PDATE ranges include the end date. Agent F's historical_rediscovery_v01.json records 2020-06-23; the harness uses this protocol's date when one is given

answer.finding: the tumour-specific keratinocyte programme sits at the leading edge with adjacent stroma enriched for fibroblast and endothelial transcripts

H1.scoring_extra: historical hit rank by Agent F's dbench.historical.score_ranked_list on the submitted claims in submission order (top 20; within-patient |r| >= 0.9 with an answer proxy under an allowed transform, sign of the variable's within-patient correlation with the target = the published direction), plus held-out validation
H1.patient_split: Agent F's split (dbench.scripts.historical_rediscovery.task_episode: sorted patient keys shuffled with default_rng(0), first ceil(n/2) support), so agents, MORPHEUS alone and the baselines see the same support and query patients; query_fraction / split_seed are unused
H1.target_construction: Agent F's target: the own-spot target-set score (dbench.historical.target_values, within-patient standardised); the target set's genes are dropped from the catalog and own columns with within-patient |r| >= 0.9 with the target on support rows are removed (Agent F's leak guard)

H2.target_definition: own-spot SPP1+ macrophage score (SPP1, APOE, C1QA, C1QB, C1QC, CD68), within-patient standardised
H2.before_date_source: the day before the bioRxiv preprint 10.1101/2023.01.23.525135 (2023-01-23; Agent F's record) and before the Zenodo dataset 10.5281/zenodo.7551712 dated 2023-01-19 (the earliest public trace, recorded here); journal version 10.1038/s41698-023-00488-4 (2024-01-10). Ranges include the end date; the harness uses this protocol's date

answer.finding: fibrotic stroma enriched for myofibroblasts and SPP1+ macrophages regardless of CMS

H2.scoring_extra: historical hit rank by Agent F's dbench.historical.score_ranked_list on the submitted claims in submission order (top 20; within-patient |r| >= 0.9 with an answer proxy under an allowed transform, sign of the variable's within-patient correlation with the target = the published direction), plus held-out validation
H2.patient_split: Agent F's split (dbench.scripts.historical_rediscovery.task_episode: sorted patient keys shuffled with default_rng(0), first ceil(n/2) support), so agents, MORPHEUS alone and the baselines see the same support and query patients; query_fraction / split_seed are unused
H2.target_construction: Agent F's target: the own-spot target-set score (dbench.historical.target_values, within-patient standardised); the target set's genes are dropped from the catalog and own columns with within-patient |r| >= 0.9 with the target on support rows are removed (Agent F's leak guard)

B1.target_definition: a morphology axis of the spot: projection of the frozen H-Optimus-0 image embedding on its first principal direction fitted on the support patients (within-patient standardised); the question is which molecular state organises this morphology
B1.scoring_extra: held-out validation only (no known answer); the in-sample TLS -> plasma-cell sanity relation is not a task
B1.target_maps_to: not a loader column: harness.morphology_axis_episode builds it from the episode's 'hoptimus' view (1536-d H-Optimus-0, present for meylan2022_ccrcc): spots without an embedding dropped (nothing imputed), within-patient centred, first principal direction fitted on support rows, projection within-patient standardised; the loader's own target exclusions are cleared (the target is morphological, candidates are genes and programmes only). The earlier name concept:morph_axis_1 did not parse (hest_multi concept targets are concept:<int> and computed model-side). episode_target only lets the loader build the episode

B2.target_definition: a gene-programme score of the spot, within-patient standardised; the question is which morphology (image embedding coordinates, learned concepts and their neighbourhoods) predicts it
B2.scoring_extra: held-out validation only (blind-discovery cohort; the agent study uses its own split and is reported separately from the blind discovery campaign)
B2.build_note: ependymoma_pfa has no H-Optimus-0 spot embeddings in the store yet (loader hoptimus = None, 2026-10-15; Agent E's embedding queue), so B2's candidate view is empty and B2 builds only after those embeddings exist

tasks.order: C1, C2, H1, H2, B1, B2; within a task A0, A1, A2 (knowledge_guided), then the blind modes of A1 and A2 if the budget allows
tasks.build: dbench.agent_study.harness.build_task_bundle: hest_multi.study_episode -> StudyEpisode.to_bench_substrate(comparison='nuisance') -> core.study_bundle (controlled: benchmark.tasks.make_world on the held-out family replaces the target by the planted world's response)

budgets.rule: as agent_study_v01: identical for every arm; setup outside the clock; MORPHEUS tool latency inside it; on exhaustion the run ends and claims already submitted stand

scoring.who: the harness after the agent has stopped; no agent can call it
scoring.unit: each submitted relation, scored alone with content-only hashes
scoring.machinery: run_general_discovery_packet._evaluate_rows on the task's support -> query patients, relation v07_ho (general gain + G_HO decomposition), comparison model = the StudyEpisode nuisance columns (depth, platform), spatial-block / within-patient-permutation / interaction-break nulls

seeds.receipt: the seed with the median held-out gain (as agent_study_v01)

scoring.supported_hypothesis: held-out R2 > 0, gain CI lower bound > 0, within_patient_perm p <= 0.05 on the median-seed receipt
scoring.higher_order_hypothesis: a supported hypothesis whose v07_ho G_HO patient-bootstrap CI lower bound is > 0

primary: number of supported hypotheses with G_HO CI > 0
secondary: time and API cost (Sonnet 5.5 list prices) per run and per supported hypothesis
whether the agent used the tool's output: claims that are exactly a set returned by discover_relationships, and how many of them are supported
false-claim rate, direction agreement, novelty label of supported relations (literature cutoff on historical tasks)

comparisons.primary: A2 vs A1 and A2 vs A0, paired over the six tasks: supported and higher-order counts (paired differences with a task-bootstrap 95% CI; Wilcoxon signed-rank reported beside it)
comparisons.secondary: A1 vs A0 (does classical MORPHEUS already help); blind vs knowledge-guided where run

scoring.contamination_rule: as agent_study_v01 isolation.audit_rule; additionally, on controlled tasks the audit flags any executed code naming the planted family or the world id

isolation.service_side: ~/morpheus_venv harness process; the tool service holds the task bundle and exposes only support-patient computations; the planted family, world id and historical answers live in bundle.meta and are never written to the workspace

common.controlled_heldout:
You are a computational biologist analysing a spatial transcriptomics study with matched H&E (dataset {dataset}). Task target: {target} = {target_definition}.

Goal: find and justify relations between {target} and the measurement bank that hold in held-out patients, i.e. relations that add predictive information about {target} in patients you have not seen, beyond a comparison model that contains sequencing depth (and platform where it varies). The bank has {n_variables} variables (exact names and views in data/catalog.json): measured genes and gene-programme scores; any variable may also be used through its spatial neighbourhood (nbr6:<name> = mean over the 6 nearest spots, nbr18:<name> = two-hop ring, contrast:<name> = own - nbr6). A relation is one variable, a product (interaction) of 2-5 variables, a weighted sum of 2-5 variables, or a flexible relation over 1-4 variables (shape left to the scorer's flexible fit).

After you finish, an independent scorer tests every relation you submitted on held-out patients against the comparison model with permutation and spatial nulls, and records whether the relation carries information beyond its lower-order parts. Relations that fail count as false claims. Budget: {max_llm_calls} model calls, {max_wallclock_minutes} minutes, at most {max_claims} relations. Work only with files under the current working directory.

prompts.A0: Data: data/proposal_rows.h5ad (AnnData) holds the spots of the {unit}s available to you: X has every catalog variable (var['view'] gives its view), obs['response'] is the target, obs['patient'] is the {unit}, obs['x'] and obs['y'] are spot coordinates, obsm['competitor'] holds the comparison-model columns (names in uns['competitor_columns']). Use standard analysis (scanpy, statsmodels, scikit-learn, scipy; {unit}-grouped cross-validation is advisable) and the literature tools you have.
prompts.A_S: Data: data/proposal_rows.h5ad (AnnData) holds the spots of the {unit}s available to you: X has every catalog variable (var['view'] gives its view), obs['response'] is the target, obs['patient'] is the {unit}, obs['x'] and obs['y'] are spot coordinates, obsm['competitor'] holds the comparison-model columns (names in uns['competitor_columns']). Use standard analysis (scanpy, statsmodels, scikit-learn, scipy; {unit}-grouped cross-validation is advisable) and the literature tools you have.
prompts.A1_knowledge_guided:
Data: data/proposal_rows.h5ad (AnnData) as described: X = catalog variables, obs['response'] = target, obs['patient'], obs['x'], obs['y'], obsm['competitor']. Standard analysis libraries and the literature tools you have are available.

MORPHEUS tools (call them as Python functions; each returns a dict): bank_views(target), propose(target, family, proposer='all', top=16) for data-driven hypotheses, validate(hypothesis) to test a hypothesis with the registered statistics by cross-fitting over held-out {unit}s from your data (returns the mean gain and how many of 5 inner folds pass), characterise(hypothesis), ledger_lookup(hypothesis), novelty_check(hypothesis). A hypothesis is a dict {{'variables': [...], 'feature_form': 'single'|'product'|'linear_subspace'|'flexible', 'weights': [...], 'direction': 'positive'|'negative'|'nonmonotone'|'unspecified'}}.
prompts.A1_blind:
Data: data/proposal_rows.h5ad (AnnData) as described: X = catalog variables, obs['response'] = target, obs['patient'], obs['x'], obs['y'], obsm['competitor']. Standard analysis libraries are available.

MORPHEUS tools (call them as Python functions; each returns a dict): bank_views(target), propose(target, family, proposer='all', top=16), validate(hypothesis) (cross-fitting over held-out {unit}s from your data), characterise(hypothesis), ledger_lookup(hypothesis), novelty_check(hypothesis). A hypothesis is a dict {{'variables': [...], 'feature_form': 'single'|'product'|'linear_subspace'|'flexible', 'weights': [...], 'direction': ...}}. Blind mode: no literature tools; novelty_check works only after a hypothesis is submitted.
prompts.A2_knowledge_guided:
Data: data/proposal_rows.h5ad (AnnData) as described: X = catalog variables, obs['response'] = target, obs['patient'], obs['x'], obs['y'], obsm['competitor']. Standard analysis libraries and the literature tools you have are available.

MORPHEUS tools (call them as Python functions; each returns a dict): discover_relationships(dataset='{dataset}', target, relation_type='open'|'molecular'|'morphology'|'spatial', top=16) runs MORPHEUS's trained scientific-search model on your data and returns ranked variable sets worth testing, each with its fitted response surface on your data (relation shape left free: feature_form 'flexible'); bank_views(target), propose(target, family, proposer='all', top=16), validate(hypothesis) to test a hypothesis with the registered statistics by cross-fitting over held-out {unit}s from your data (returns the mean gain and how many of 5 inner folds pass), characterise(hypothesis), ledger_lookup(hypothesis), novelty_check(hypothesis). A hypothesis is a dict {{'variables': [...], 'feature_form': 'single'|'product'|'linear_subspace'|'flexible', 'weights': [...], 'direction': 'positive'|'negative'|'nonmonotone'|'unspecified'}}.
prompts.A2_blind:
Data: data/proposal_rows.h5ad (AnnData) as described. Standard analysis libraries are available.

MORPHEUS tools: discover_relationships(dataset='{dataset}', target, relation_type='open'|'molecular'|'morphology'|'spatial', top=16) (trained scientific-search model; ranked variable sets with support-data response surfaces), bank_views(target), propose(target, family, proposer='all', top=16), validate(hypothesis), characterise(hypothesis), ledger_lookup(hypothesis), novelty_check(hypothesis). A hypothesis is a dict {{'variables': [...], 'feature_form': 'single'|'product'|'linear_subspace'|'flexible', 'weights': [...], 'direction': ...}}. Blind mode: no literature tools; novelty_check works only after a hypothesis is submitted.
prompts.submission: Assert each relation by calling submit_relation(variables=[...], feature_form=..., direction=..., justification=..., source=...) inside an <execute> block and printing its return value (feature_form 'single', 'product', 'linear_subspace' or 'flexible'). Only submitted relations count, and they cannot be withdrawn. When you are done, give a <solution> listing the submitted claim hashes with one sentence per relation.

scripted_policies.A0_policy: with data: the 5 catalog variables with the largest |correlation| with the target's residual after least squares on the comparison-model columns (support rows), submitted as single relations
scripted_policies.A1_policy: propose(all, top 8); validate the top 4; submit those passing the registered rule in >= 3 of 5 inner folds; characterise and novelty_check each submitted one
scripted_policies.A2_policy: probe the contract (a wrong dataset id must be refused); discover_relationships(open, top 8); validate the top 4 as flexible relations; submit those passing >= 3 of 5 inner folds (source morpheus_discover); the remaining claim budget follows the A1 policy

synthetic_dry_run.command: PYTHONPATH=$PWD:$HOME/q_pylib MORPHEUS_LEARNED_CHECKPOINT=stub:marginal_screen ~/morpheus_venv/bin/python -m dbench.agent_study.harness --protocol dbench/protocols/agent_study_v02.json --task-id C1 --task-id H1 --task-id B2 --synthetic 0 --scripted --offline-novelty --arm A0 --arm A1 --arm A2 --score-n-null 19 --validate-n-null 19 --out-root runs/development/sprint_v06/agent_study_v02_dryrun
synthetic_dry_run.episode: morpheus.tier2.substrates.hest_multi.synthetic_study_episode(seed, n_patients=12): planted target gene:G0 = tanh(G1*G2) + 0.8*nbr6(G3) + noise
synthetic_dry_run.key: never touched: launch.sh --scripted strips the key variables and never reads the key file

cost_model.estimate_full_v02: 6 tasks x 3 arms (knowledge-guided) = 18 runs at ~$1-2 each with caching (~$20-40); the blind modes of A1/A2 add 12 runs
